name: Carrow & Fenn Waxed Dispatch Jacket
description:
A heavy waxed-cotton jacket in the tradition of working outerwear, built by a mid-tier label that has been making durable goods in the Milwaukee basin for three generations. The cut is boxy and honest — two chest pockets, two hand-pockets with storm flaps, a corduroy collar that softens with age. The wax finish darkens at the elbows and cuffs over time, developing a patina that makes each jacket unique to its owner. Available in dark olive, tobacco brown, and a deep navy that almost reads black under artificial light.

This is a jacket people buy once and wear for a decade. It smells faintly of beeswax and lanolin. It does not have any embedded systems, no climate layer, no signal shielding — it is simply very well made. Courier workers, warehouse supervisors, and off-duty mechanics reach for it on cold mornings. It is the kind of jacket that accumulates patches and pins without looking cluttered.
what_it_says: You value durability over novelty. You probably fix things rather than replacing them. You have worn this jacket through rain and did not care.
worn_by: Tier 2 regulars who distrust fast fashion
story_hooks: A courier's Carrow & Fenn jacket contains a hidden interior pocket sewn shut — something was sealed inside it before the original owner disappeared
A Tier 3 character is embarrassed to admit they bought one after their expensive corp jacket failed them in a rainstorm
The wax finish on a particular batch from three years ago was accidentally contaminated with a mild bioluminescent compound — those jackets glow faintly green in total darkness

physical_description.visual_profile: A substantial, boxy silhouette that reads as honest and utilitarian. The jacket hangs straight from the shoulders with minimal taper, giving it a timeless working-class presence. It sits at hip-length with a structured stance—neither aggressive nor apologetic. Worn examples develop a rich patina at stress points that adds character rather than detracting from it.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and intentionally generous through the chest and torso. Cut to layer comfortably over cargo thermals or reinforced undershirts. Sleeves are straight and slightly long, designed to cover wrists when arms hang at rest. No compression or athletic shaping—this is a garment built for movement and durability, not silhouette.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy waxed cotton (canvas-weight base). The wax finish is applied by hand in the Milwaukee basin workshop, using traditional lanolin and beeswax formulas. Weight and hand suggest heritage craftsmanship rather than synthetic optimization.
physical_description.texture: Initially stiff and waxy with a subtle sheen. With wear, the surface softens and develops micro-creasing. Elbows and cuff edges darken to deep chocolate or near-black through repeated flexing and contact, creating natural burnishing. The corduroy collar starts structured and gradually relaxes into soft waves.
physical_description.color_scheme: Three core options: dark olive (muted, tactical-adjacent but working-class), tobacco brown (warm, aging beautifully to cognac), deep navy (reads almost black under neon but reveals depth in daylight). All develop richer, darker patinas with age. No logos or bold graphic elements—just honest material.
physical_description.closures: Traditional button front—heavy horn or corozo buttons, slightly oversized, spaced generously for gloved operation. Hand pockets and chest pockets feature storm flaps with snap closures. Heavy-duty construction means no delicate mechanisms.
distinctive_features: Two large chest pockets with storm flaps and snap closures
Two deep hand-pockets with flap covers for tool/cargo storage
Corduroy collar that softens and darkens with age
Reinforced elbow patches (natural wear areas that accelerate darkening)
Honest, generous seaming throughout—stitching is visible and intentional
No interior branding beyond a woven Carrow & Fenn label
Designed to accept pins, patches, and custom modifications without looking chaotic
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional with Tier 2 heritage premium. A jacket that costs what a mid-tier worker makes in 2-3 weeks, but the manufacturing lineage and reputation elevate it above disposable fast-fashion. It signals investment in quality, not flash.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by courier drivers navigating GLMZ cold zones, warehouse supervisors, off-duty mechanics, and anyone who respects tools and craft. Suggests someone who expects to own their clothes for a decade, not a season. Anti-status statement—wears exactly the same whether you're Tier 3 or disguised Tier 1.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in after first season. Develops visible creasing at elbows, shoulders, and waist. Typically carries 2-4 custom patches or pins by year three (courier guild markers, memorial patches, mechanical certifications). Wax darkening at edges becomes pronounced by year two. Still functional and water-resistant after heavy use. Accumulates a faint oil and beeswax smell that deepens with age.
